expectation: The mesh will join the lined air sacs to form an exchange surface for air and blood.

reason: The pleural membranes connect the lung side to the chest side through a sealed fluid gap, so they appear to be the next piece needed for breathing.
expectation: The membranes will attach to the lung route so the chest can help move it.

reaction: The result makes the remaining connection clear.
reason: The breathing chest can couple to the outer pleural sheet and renew the air in the sacs.
expectation: Chest movement will renew the air in the lung sacs, supporting continued oxygen exchange.

effect: The moving chest completed the oxygen-delivering circulation, linking renewed lung air to oxygen delivery at body tissues.
reaction: The full route from lungs to body and back is a satisfying conclusion to the construction.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lung route to the blood circuit was most worthwhile: the result showed both how blood reaches the exchange surface and why still air must be renewed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lining and then the capillary mesh felt somewhat sequential and predictable, though the separate parts made the two sides of the exchange surface clear.

surprise.text: The shrinking oxygen arrows as still air lost oxygen clarified why circulation alone cannot sustain oxygen uptake.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each part had a visible connection to the goal.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because connecting the lung and circulation systems made me curious about how the body supplies other materials to working cells. The largely predictable assembly would be more engaging if later chapters offered more meaningful choices.
